Democrats are set to take the Senate majority in the next Congress.

President Donald Trump pressed lawmakers to pass the SAVE America Act before the midterms. The legislation failed to advance before Election Day.

The bill would require proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections. In May, a Rasmussen Reports survey found that 63% of likely US voters support the SAVE Act, including 45% who strongly support it. Thirty-one percent oppose the bill. It also found broader agreement on the underlying principle. Eighty-four percent of respondents said only US citizens should be allowed to vote in US elections, while 10% disagreed. Rasmussen also reported that 52% of likely voters believe noncitizens are likely illegally registered to vote in their state, including 31% who said it is very likely. Thirty-eight percent said they consider it unlikely.

Rasmussen found that 84% of Republicans back the SAVE Act, compared to 64% of unaffiliated voters and 42% of Democrats.

Support for voter ID requirements in general runs higher. CNN data analyst Harry Enten said earlier this year that voter ID is "not controversial," citing polling that showed 83% of Americans support it. Enten also noted that support crosses lines of political affiliation and race.

"The bottom line is this: Voter ID is not controversial in this country," Enten concluded. "A photo ID to vote is not controversial in this country. It is not controversial by party, and it is not controversial by race."

Americans agree with Nicki Minaj when it comes to voter id. 

83% of favor photo voter id to vote per Pew. This includes 70%+ of Democrats and Republicans, as well as 75%+ of Americans across races.... White, Black, and Latino. 

It's not controversial. pic.twitter.com/9Kocw85Uh8

— (((Harry Enten))) (@ForecasterEnten) February 3, 2026

Back in March, Florida passed its Voter ID law, and Oklahoma followed suit in August, approving a voter ID measure 54.6% to 45.4%, months ahead of the general election.

Even as Democrats rode a blue wave on Election Day, election integrity measures quietly racked up wins, often by lopsided margins.

In Nevada, Question 7, which requires photo ID for in-person voting and identification numbers on mail ballots, passed 62.2%-37.9%. North Carolina voters extended the photo ID requirement already in the state constitution to mail ballots, and Ohio wrote its existing voter ID rules into its own constitution, making them much harder for future legislatures or courts to undo.

The citizenship question was even more one-sided. Measures reinforcing that only citizens can vote passed in four states: Arkansas, Kansas, South Dakota, West Virginia. Alaska also approved a citizenship requirement as state law. The wins bring the number of states with explicit constitutional prohibitions on noncitizen voting to 22.

Despite these victories, not every state got on board. Voter ID measures failed in California (60.4%-39.6%), Colorado (63.3%-36.7%), and Arizona, where Proposition 144, which also would have reinforced citizenship requirements, lost 53.3%-46.7%.

Still, in a year when the political winds blew hard against Republicans, voters in red and purple states alike made clear that asking people to prove who they are, and that they're citizens, isn't a partisan idea.

items.title: Watch: What Hegseth's Entourage Did At The Tomb Of The Unknown Soldier That Made A Sentinel Shout

Watch: What Hegseth's Entourage Did At The Tomb Of The Unknown Soldier That Made A Sentinel Shout

A US Army sentinel guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier reprimanded Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, his wife and a group of his senior advisers on Wednesday after some in the party laughed and chatted beside the memorial following the Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery.

"All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times," the sentinel called out across the plaza, in footage CNN aired live Wednesday afternoon.

Hegseth had been posing for photos in front of the tomb with his wife, Jennifer, chief of staff Ricky Buria, deputy chief of staff Patrick Weaver and senior adviser Tami Radabaugh when the laughter started, according to CNN. The footage doesn't show who in the group laughed, or whether Hegseth was one of them.

The group had spent the morning at the wreath-laying with President Trump and Vice President JD Vance, a day after the House voted Tuesday night to send Rep. Thomas Massie's eight articles of impeachment against him back to the Judiciary Committee, which effectively shelves the effort until Democrats take over the chamber in January, as we reported.

"Now, we should be clear, this is something that happens if people are at the tomb," CNN anchor Brianna Keilar told viewers, and CNN's Zachary Cohen added that anyone who breaks the silence "will get similarly reprimanded by the Army Sentinel who is guarding the tomb at the time."

At each changing of the guard, the relief commander "faces the spectators and asks them to stand and remain silent during the ceremony," according to the cemetery's own description of the ritual.

Soldiers of the 3rd US Infantry Regiment, The Old Guard, have stood watch over the tomb since April 6, 1948, and it has been guarded around the clock since 1937. Its earliest guards were there to keep visitors from climbing or stepping on the tomb, according to the cemetery's history of the memorial. The tomb holds an unknown American killed in World War I.

The Army said an Arlington employee who tried to stop Trump campaign staff from filming in Section 60 in August 2024 was pushed aside, in the part of the cemetery where troops killed in Iraq and Afghanistan are buried. The campaign disputed that account, and the Army later released a heavily redacted report on the incident, as we noted at the time.

When a sentinel shoulders arms, the rifle goes on the shoulder closest to the visitors, which Arlington says signifies that the guard "stands between the Tomb and any possible threat."

Middle East Oil Flows Far From Normal Despite Signs Of Oversupply

Authored by Tsvetana Paraskova via OilPrice,

  • Middle Eastern crude exports have recovered to near pre-war levels, raising fears of an oil glut and pushing Brent down roughly 17% in five trading days.
  • Record tanker rates and war insurance premiums remain a major burden, with crude transport costs reaching $30 per barrel despite weakening oil prices.
  • Depleted global inventories and disrupted fuel exports threaten a sustained recovery, with industry leaders warning that rebuilding oil stocks could take up to two years.

Crude oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz and the whole Middle Eastern region have recovered to close to pre-war levels, vessel-tracking services have been signaling for over a month now.

Middle Eastern benchmarks have been weakening for weeks, suggesting an oil glut may be building amid rebounding Persian Gulf exports and global demand destruction amid high prices.

On the face of it, an oversupply of crude oil could be forming. But the costs to refiners and consumers are not falling. War, insurance premiums, and record tanker rates have raised the cost of transporting a barrel of crude oil from about $5 per barrel before the war to as much as $30 a barrel, and at times even higher.

Middle Eastern producers are forced to slash their official selling prices to win customers because the surge in Persian Gulf exports is weakening the physical prices of local grades. Moreover, amid high freight costs, Middle East's crude oil could only win Asia's price-sensitive buyers with lower prices.

Shock Not Over

The pricing of the Middle Eastern barrels and the weakening market structure of the benchmark Middle East crudes signal an oil glut is forming.

But the shock to the global oil and fuel markets isn't over as increased flows don't mean traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has suddenly become less dangerous. In fact, attacks on vessels have intensified in the past month, while producers are tying up a large portion of the global tanker fleet on inefficient shuttle movements in and out of the Strait and subsequent ship-to-ship (STS) transfers in the Gulf of Oman.

Normal oil trade patterns from before the Iran war may never return. Until the market adapts to the new normal and Gulf producers build alternative supply routes, the war and insurance premium risks will remain with crude flows.

Hopes are high again in the past few days that the U.S. and Iran could reach an agreement, amid signals that President Donald Trump could pursue diplomacy instead of escalation following the crushing defeat in the U.S. midterm elections. In the past five trading days after the elections, Brent Crude prices slumped by about 17% to trade just above $91 per barrel early on Tuesday.

The market has been blindsided by sudden breakdowns of attempts at talks on several occasions in the past eight months. The relative calmness after the elections in the U.S. and Israel, which weren't positive for either Trump or Benjamin Netanyahu, may be only transitory.

Weaker Middle East Oil Prices

Regardless, the perceived near-term glut is pressuring the Middle East's crude oil prices.

The curve of the Dubai benchmark signaled last week that rising oil flows from the Middle East are exceeding demand for the first time since early July, when the three-week U.S.-Iran ceasefire allowed millions of barrels to leave unhindered the Strait of Hormuz. The November contract of the Dubai grade was in contango early last week, suggesting that concerns about the immediate lack of crude supply have eased significantly.

Rising supply from the Middle East has also weakened both the Dubai and Murban prices. At the end of October, the prices of physical Middle East crude slumped as flows from the region are recovering and reaching pre-war levels on some days.

Saudi oil giant Aramco last week slashed the price for its flagship Arab Light crude for Asia for loading in December by $2 per barrel, to a discount of $6.50 per barrel to the Oman/Dubai average. This is the steepest discount to the Middle East's benchmark since May 2020 during the COVID pandemic.

Yet the cost to move the crude out of the region is very high - freight rates remain elevated amid a shortage of tankers and still sizeable war insurance premiums.

Normalization is further off in fuel exports out of the Middle East.

"Middle East crude exports have returned to pre-war levels, while refined product flows remain at just 37% of normal," Ole Hansen, Head of Commodity Strategy at Saxo Bank, said in a note last week.

"For now, the market is trading on hopes of a breakthrough rather than concrete evidence that an agreement is close. The two sides may still be far apart on important issues, leaving the outlook highly uncertain," Hansen added.

"Without sustained positive signals from both Washington and Tehran, the recent decline could prove vulnerable to a reversal."

Depleted Inventories Could Boost Post-War Demand

Even if the Iran and Ukraine wars were to be settled with lasting peace agreements by the end of the year, the glut narrative may not hold because global inventories have depleted so much that it would take months, and probably a few years, to bring them back to adequate levels.

"Re-filling inventories while meeting demand could take up to two years," Saudi Aramco's CEO Amin Nasser said at an energy conference in Riyadh last month.

The chief executive of another major Middle Eastern national oil company, ADNOC, last week warned that diesel stocks in some markets have slumped to their lowest seasonal levels in 35 years.

The global energy system needs to be more resilient as the Middle East crisis has forced nearly 1 billion barrels of crude draws from inventories, ADNOC's chief executive Sultan Al Jaber said at the ADIPEC 2026 energy conference in Abu Dhabi.

"Simply put, the world has eroded its supply buffers," Al Jaber said.

Nvidia Preparing To Fire Huang After 2nd Affair Bombshell, Stock Knifes Lower: Report

*** Update: NVIDIA PREPARING TO OUST NVIDIA CEO JENSEN HUANG: WSJ 

Nvidia is reportedly preparing to remove founder and CEO Jensen Huang following revelations of two extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese intelligence operative.The board could meet as soon as today to decide Huang's future, according to people familiar with the matter. No final decision or official announcement has been confirmed.

The chipmaker is scheduled to report quarterly results on Nov. 17. 

It “will be interesting how it handles next week’s earnings call. Their CFO [Colette Kress] can handle the numbers but markets will want more on changes to the governance,” said Dec Mullarkey of SLC Management. 

Who would replace him?

~~~~~~

Jensen Huang, the Nvidia chief already under a board investigation over his affair with a woman US intelligence says is a Chinese spy, also had an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, according to five people who worked at the company and spoke to The New York Times.

According to the people, the executive is Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care. Huang, 63, and Powell, 48, are both married to other people, and the relationship has been discussed inside the company, the five said.

Two of the people told the paper that the pair were caught on video being affectionate at a San Jose hotel in March, during GTC, Nvidia's annual developer conference, while company executives were meeting nearby. Three people briefed on the incident said a bystander filmed the moment on their phone, and that Huang's security spotted the bystander, sequestered them and offered them a nondisclosure agreement. The Times says it has not seen the video.

When the paper reached Huang by phone on Wednesday and asked him about Powell, he replied: "I don't think you should be talking to me directly." Then he hung up. Nvidia declined to provide a statement.

Nvidia's own code of conduct tells employees to avoid situations where their actions "create conflict," and it lists "personal relationships" among them. The company also says it "promptly investigates reports of misconduct." Many large corporations bar managers from relationships with subordinates.

Shares were displeased after hours (NVDA -8% from the close to its lowest since July 2025):

"It is going to be a very challenging situation," said Michael O’Rourke, chief market strategist at Jonestrading. "Jensen had forecast 70% sales growth this year. With the vendor financing and the aggressive tactics, his successor will spend the next year putting out fires and cleaning up messes." 

"If these allegations are confirmed by the independent investigation, one has to expect the board to remove him. That is the standard for corporate governance today. Even worse this is a pattern," he added. 

While the odds of Huang resigning spiked on Polymarket.

Powell joined Nvidia in 2008 to bring its GPUs into medical imaging instruments. According to her LinkedIn, she was promoted to senior director of AI business development in 2016, and by late 2017 she was vice president of health care, overseeing programs that apply Nvidia's chips to higher education and health care. She speaks for the company at technology conferences around the world; at GTC in March she gave a talk on AI-driven breakthroughs in health care and biology, with slides that used cartoon versions of Huang.

As we reported on Oct. 29, US officials identified Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, as a Chinese intelligence asset after Huang grew close to her; Beijing has denied the espionage claims. On Nov. 8 Huang admitted the affair in a memo to staff: "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did," he wrote.

That same day Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation, which the Times says is being led by the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. The board said it had "no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised."

Meanwhile, the Republican chairs of the House Foreign Affairs, China Select and Intelligence committees have asked Huang for a closed-door briefing on Nov. 18 about his dealings with Alice Huang, and gave him until Nov. 11 to answer. Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast said he is prepared to subpoena Huang if he doesn't respond by Wednesday, the same day the Powell report landed.

Investors have already been rattled: Nvidia shares slid on Nov. 9 after the board's probe was announced. Nvidia reports third-quarter earnings on Nov. 17, the day before Huang's requested appearance on Capitol Hill.

items.title: Trump And Texas' New Democrat Governor Are Headed For War Over The Border
items.content_text:
Trump And Texas' New Democrat Governor Are Headed For War Over The Border

The midterms did more than change which party will control Congress for the next year. By electing Gina Hinojosa governor, Texas voters ended a decade-long partnership between Austin and Washington on the border and set the state on a collision course with the Trump administration over immigration enforcement.

President Trump said Thursday that he will step in if Texas' incoming Democratic administration abandons the state's role in border enforcement. A reporter put the question to him directly in the Oval Office.

"Are you ready to reinforce the Texas southern border now that democratic, the new democratic governor is removing state manpower from border defense?" the reporter asked.

"I am sure that the new governor is going to want to have security of this Texas border," Trump said. "There were people on television two days ago saying how it's like living in heaven compared to living in hell when Biden was there. And I'm sure they'll continue my policy. And if they don't continue my policy, I will."

Democrats in Texas also captured the attorney general's office and flipped the Texas House, giving the party control over the levers that have made Texas the federal government's most important state partner on immigration. Republicans held the Texas Senate.

Gov. Greg Abbott (R-TX) launched Operation Lone Star and committed substantial state resources to border security, including border barriers, additional law enforcement deployments, immigration detention capacity, and transporting migrants to Democratic-led cities. The Trump administration adopted several of Abbott's strategies and has relied on Texas for substantial help with enforcement. Texas maintains more extensive state and local cooperation with federal immigration authorities than any other state.

Despite its success, Hinojosa has dismissed Operation Lone Star as "political theatre" and insists it is an expensive waste of taxpayer money. She has already made it clear she intends to review the operation's budget and may scale back or dismantle portions of it.

The National Guard gives her another lever. About 1,400 Guard members from 17 states currently support the Department of Homeland Security and Immigration and Customs Enforcement with logistical, transportation, and administrative work. Governors retain control over their states' Guard personnel, which would allow Hinojosa to pull Texas troops out of the federal mission.

Trump allies say losing Texas' cooperation would seriously undermine federal enforcement, particularly during another border crisis. White House advisers, including Stephen Miller, the architect of the administration's enforcement policy and Trump's new chief of staff, are expected to press Austin to keep working with federal authorities. Concern has also reached agents in the field.

"I fear that now Texas will bar any law enforcement working with us like they do in California," one Border Patrol agent told the Washington Examiner last week.

The attorney general's office is the second pressure point. Incoming Attorney General Nathan Johnson (D-TX) plans to review agreements between Texas law enforcement agencies and ICE and has questioned the federal 287(g) program, which lets state and local police assist with immigration enforcement.

César Cuauhtémoc García Hernández, an immigration attorney from the Rio Grande Valley and a law professor at Ohio State University, said Johnson's win carries as much weight as Hinojosa's.

"Ken Paxton has been at the forefront of working hand-in-hand with Republican leaders of other states, and more recently with the Trump administration, to make Texas the model of harsh immigration policies," he said.

Local governments have already moved. Houston Mayor John Whitmire limited cooperation between city police and ICE during traffic stops, citing community trust and public safety. The change came after an ICE officer fatally shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a Mexican construction worker, in July.

Opponents of immigration enforcement clearly see the midterm elections in Texas as a referendum on Trump's immigration policies.

"We have had enough, get ICE out of our communities," said Osvaldo Grimaldo, policy strategist on border and immigrants' rights at the ACLU of Texas, describing what he called the message from voters "along the border and throughout the state."

Edna Yang, co-executive director of the Austin-based group American Gateways, said she sees the results as a reaction to anger after "witnessing the cruelty towards immigrants that has been going on for the last two or so years."

Democrats claim they intend to keep the border secure, and will only end practices they consider excessive. Rep. Joaquin Castro (D-TX) said Hinojosa could reshape how enforcement operates in the state. Advocates expect changes but say they will take time, and Rochelle Garza of the Texas Civil Rights Project urged Democrats to act on their win. "And frankly, if it's not seized upon, it can be lost," she said.

But despite the Democrats' victories, there are limits on what can be done, especially since Republicans still control the state Senate.

Kristin Etter, director of policy and legal services at the Texas Immigration Law Council, outlined the limits on the new administration.

"Obviously, a new state governor can't rewrite immigration laws, but Texas can make a difference in terms of the choices they make about how it uses its state resources," she said.

State law stands as the largest obstacle to any pivot. A measure Abbott signed last year requires sheriffs in the 234 Texas counties that run jails to enter agreements with ICE allowing their officers to assist federal enforcement, and most counties have complied. With Republicans controlling the Senate, Democrats lack the votes to repeal it.

The Department of Homeland Security has not said whether its operations in Texas will change. "It's too soon to tell," a DHS official told CNN.

items.title: Meta's AI Will Now Guess Your Age On Instagram... Even If You Say You're An Adult
items.content_text:
Meta's AI Will Now Guess Your Age On Instagram... Even If You Say You're An Adult

Authored by Naveen Athrappully via The Epoch Times,

Meta Platforms is expanding its AI-powered age-estimation technology to identify Instagram users suspected of being teenagers, even if they registered with an adult birthdate, and automatically apply stricter safety settings to their accounts.

Meta said in a Nov. 9 statement that the expansion will mean millions more teenagers worldwide will receive Teen Account protections, offering built-in safeguards that automatically limit the content they see, time spent on the app, and who can contact them.

We're expanding the AI technology we use to help ensure teens are in the right experiences for their age globally. https://t.co/G97qdcqJOO

— Meta Newsroom (@MetaNewsroom) November 9, 2026

Starting this month, U.S. parents on Instagram will receive a notification explaining how Meta will apply the age-appropriate protections for teens and how they can help ensure that their teenage child is logged in with the correct age, Meta said.

Meta uses AI and other signals to estimate a user's age, including information from profiles, comments, posts, captions, and bios, such as references to school grades or birthdays, Larry Magid, CEO of nonprofit ConnectSafely, wrote in a Nov. 6 post on Meta's website.

The company can also analyze photo and video visual patterns to determine a person's age.

"This visual analysis is not facial recognition. The idea is to look for general visual characteristics that suggest someone who is underage that may help estimate an age range, not to identify the person," Magid said. "Meta deactivates suspected under-13 accounts and requires proof of age to prevent deletion."

Teens aged 13 to 15 require parental permission to make some of their account protections less restrictive. Those aged 16 and 17 will have more freedom to update certain settings but will still face restrictions, such as content limitations, that cannot be changed without parental permission.

Meta said it is continuing to roll out the technology on Facebook and later this year will begin launching similar measures globally on Threads.

The company said it has also started using Apple's age-range signal in Australia as an additional method to help determine users' ages.

"When a parent sets up a smartphone for their teen, they have the option for the app store to confirm the age of the person using the device and assign them an age range," the company said. "Then, each time the teen downloads an app, Apple passes that age range to the developer - Meta, for example - confirming whether the teen meets the app's age requirement."

The expansion of protections for teenage Instagram users comes after Meta reached a roughly $18.1 billion settlement with multiple U.S. jurisdictions in August over allegations of endangering children.

The agreement settles a series of lawsuits brought against Meta, accusing the company of intentionally designing its platforms to be addictive, knowingly exposing children to mental harms, and misleading people about the safety of its offerings.

As part of the settlement, Meta agreed to institute age-verification protocols and content controls, as well as time limits for children.

Meta agreed to pay $17.1 billion to settle lawsuits brought by 47 U.S. states, territories, and the District of Columbia, and $1 billion to settle a lawsuit from Texas.

California Lawsuit

Meta recently filed a lawsuit seeking to block California from enforcing a new state law that aims to protect children under 16 from the negative effects of social media exposure.

Assembly Bill 1709 prohibits online platforms from offering underage children features deemed to be psychologically exploitative that could result in compulsive use. This includes sending videos through autoplay features and offering personal recommendations. Platforms are obligated to delete the accounts of children with such features.

Meta, Google, and TikTok filed separate lawsuits on Nov. 4, seeking to stop the bill's implementation and alleging that the measure violates First Amendment free speech protections.

Advocacy group Electronic Privacy Information Center (EPIC) welcomed the bill in a Sept. 1 statement, saying it strongly supports social media regulations aimed at keeping children safe online.

"With AB 1709, California takes the right approach to protecting kids online," said Megan Iorio, director of EPIC's platform governance and accountability program.

"Design features that manipulate kids are the problem. Prohibiting these features, as AB 1709 does, provides a solution that is effective and does not infringe on kids' rights to access digital spaces."

items.title: David Sacks Sounds Alarm Over Democrats' Most Terrifying Censorship Plan Yet
items.content_text:
David Sacks Sounds Alarm Over Democrats' Most Terrifying Censorship Plan Yet

David Sacks, who stepped down as President Trump's AI and crypto czar in March, says it's "100%" that the Democrats who just won Congress will make a major push for AI legislation, and that the end state is "a surveillance and censorship state that's turbocharged by superintelligence."

Sacks was answering co-host Jason Calacanis on the All-In podcast released Nov. 7. Calacanis asked for odds on a scenario co-host David Friedberg had laid out, in which only the government can use the tools. Sacks said he didn't think it would go that far, then laid out the road map he does expect: "You create a department, a federal department of AI. You require that all the so-called frontier models have to be reviewed and approved by that."

"The regulators give their notes on it. You can't get a model released unless you address their concerns," Sacks said. Those concerns, in his telling, would be "disinformation and misinformation and dissonant thought" - "all the things that the government was pressuring the social media companies to crack down on and censor during COVID."

"They're going to basically reenact that whole regime again using AI. And it's going to be infinitely more powerful because we're talking about superintelligence here," Sacks said. "So I do believe that that is the regime that we're headed towards."

David Sacks predicts Democrats will use AI legislation and frontier-model approvals to create a surveillance and censorship state 'turbocharged by superintelligence'

"It's 100% that Democrats are going to make a major push for AI legislation in the next Congress. The question is... https://t.co/QQ0aASM7gX pic.twitter.com/x1WJMipb4i

— Fireside Alpha (@firesidealpha) November 7, 2026

The warning came four days after Democrats swept the midterms. According to Reuters, Democrats plan a wave of AI and data-center bills when they take control in January, among them a push by Rep. Lori Trahan (D-Mass.) to have independent experts test leading AI models against safety standards and rules on when AI companies can be held liable for harm. Rep. Ted Lieu (D-Calif.) has promised hearings and "reasonable guardrails on AI," accusing Trump and congressional Republicans of a "conscious decision" to "let the AI industry run wild."

Michigan's Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed ran on something close to the department Sacks describes. His campaign's "AI Under Control" plan calls for "A Cabinet-Level, Independent AI Safety Agency," which it sums up as "One agency with the power to inspect labs, block releases, and order a pause or command a shutdown." When he released it in October, El-Sayed said, "At an absolute minimum, I'm calling for a pause in AI frontier development."

Before the election, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, Commerce Committee Chairman Ted Cruz and Sen. Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.) were already negotiating a bipartisan bill, as we reported in September. Negotiators aim to give the US government "the power to block the release of certain AI models that are deemed unsafe," Reuters reported, with companies able to challenge that decision in federal court. In the House, Lieu and Rep. Nathaniel Moran (R-Texas) filed an AI Kill Switch Act that would let the Homeland Security secretary order AI products throttled, suspended or shut down, as we noted in July.

Trump's own Commerce Department knocked two frontier models offline in June. A national-security directive from Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's office cut off foreign nationals' access to Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 on June 12; unable to check users' citizenship, the company blocked everyone, after what it says was about 90 minutes' warning and no specifics, as we reported. Sacks made the administration's case the next day, saying "the ball is in Anthropic's court."

I've had a number of conversations with folks inside and outside government about the current situation with Anthropic, and here is what I believe to be true: 

- As we know, Anthropic publicly released its Mythos class models earlier this week under the commercial name Fable....

— David Sacks (@DavidSacks) June 13, 2026

Access came back about three weeks later, after Lutnick said Commerce had "worked closely with Anthropic to analyze and approve Fable 5 to ensure alignment across the US Government," as we reported. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had also helped develop a plan for a FINRA-style regulator, reporting to the SEC, that would "vet the safety" of AI models, according to a July report.

Sacks has accused Democrats before of plotting to push "woke AI" through state laws. As czar, he told Fox Business last December, "We don't like seeing blue states trying to insert their woke ideology in AI models, and we really want to try and stop that," and said Colorado's ban on "algorithmic discrimination," which makes AI developers liable for a model's "disparate impact," "raises very serious First Amendment concerns."

Alphabet put the COVID pressure he points to on the record in September 2025, calling the Biden administration's pressure over content "unacceptable and wrong" in a letter to House Judiciary Chairman Jim Jordan, according to the committee, and offering creators banned over COVID and election speech a way back onto YouTube, as we reported.

Trump can veto whatever the new Congress sends him, and overriding him takes two-thirds of both chambers. "The probability of legislation is much higher than people anticipate," Raymond James analyst Ed Mills told Reuters, noting that Democrats could try to attach AI rules to routine must-pass bills.

items.title: When A Society Has Reached Its Limits, Reforms No Longer Fix What's Broken
items.content_text:
When A Society Has Reached Its Limits, Reforms No Longer Fix What's Broken

Authored by Charles Hugh Smith via OfTwoMinds blog,

The most difficult part of my framework to grasp is the keystone: our system has reached its limits. The difficulty is that this is impossible to understand if one is embedded in the system's beliefs of how the world works and wedded to the system's sclerosis via self-interest.

Once self-interest dominates, it locks the system into its current configuration because attempting to change anything rouses resistance from whatever interests depend on that part of the status quo for their piece of the pie.

The sustainability of the entire system is of no concern because the only thing that matters is keeping our piece of the pie intact as-is. Nothing can change because that threatens somebody's share of the pie, i.e. how the system distributes income, gains, power and risk.

Everyone from the super-wealthy to low-income households fears any change that might reduce their security. Beneath our everyday awareness, a balance has been struck: if we just keep this exact arrangement as-is, everyone accepts the status quo.

This rigidity leads to sclerosis: the system has lost the flexibility and nimbleness needed to adapt. Any proposal that actually changes the socio-economic system is immediately struck off by those whose interests are threatened.

This leads to the substitution of artifice for authenticity - the other core concept that is impossible to understand if one is wedded to the status quo by self-interest and the fear of losing what we have.

Once a system has reached the point where authentic change becomes impossible because it disrupts the delicate balance of self-interest, it has reached its limits, and is set on run to failure, for a system that has lost its adaptive flexibility is doomed once conditions change.

Rather than face this disruptive reality, everyone wedded to the existing balance becomes dependent on expediencies that keep the system glued together, but at the cost of system stability. As self-interest and sclerosis dominate, the focus narrows to doing whatever it takes to maintain the increasingly unsustainable balance of interests.

This is how we've reached the point where the federal government borrows $2 trillion a year - 27% of its entire outlays - to maintain the precarious balance of every interest group. That this is unsustainable is obvious, but since real change is impossible because of the system's limits, everyone approves of expediencies that only add to the destabilizing momentum of run to failure.

The system no longer considers truly new ideas, as these threaten the delicate balance of self-interests. Just as expediencies are artifice, so too are the cover stories masking the unsustainability of expediencies. To avoid facing the impossibility of the status quo continuing unchanged, all public dialog is reduced to cliches, delusions and fantasies.

These artifices create an illusion of stability and sustainability that I call The Big Con, a mindset in which everything is fake but this is all that's acceptable. So the tired cliches of capitalism and socialism are deployed as rallying cries or cudgels, with no actual understanding of what they mean because that would get in the way of the "message:" what's needed are fake facades and fantasies, not understanding.

This dependence on parodies, cliches, delusions and fantasies to maintain the illusion of sustainability is also called hyper-normalization: we accept the unsustainable as permanent because this is what the system incentivizes and rewards.

The system has reached its limits on every level: institutional, conceptual and structural. The incentives to maintain the facades that everything is working just fine and policy tweaks / technology wil fix whatever's broken and the disincentives to tell the truth are kept firmly in place by self-interest, even though these lock the system as a whole in run to failure.

This leads to extremes that destabilize the system from inside: extremes of wealth-power inequality, extremes of fantasy (technology and finance can fix all problems) and artifice that lead to where we are today, with absurdly transparent parodies and self-parodies being presented as serious solutions proposed by serious people.

Scholar / author Ray Huang (no relation to Jensen) summed this up in his book 1587, A Year of No Significance: The Ming Dynasty in Decline that traced how the Ming Dynasty reaching its internal limits led to its inevitable collapse:

"The year 1587 may seem to be insignificant; nevertheless, it is evident by that time the limit for the Ming dynasty had already been reached. It no longer mattered whether the ruler was conscientious or irresponsible, whether his chief counselor was enterprising or conformist, whether the generals were resourceful or incompetent, whether the civil officials were honest or corrupt, or whether the leading thinkers were radicals or conservatives - in the end they all failed to reach fulfillment."

But why can't the system regain control of these runaway forces? The answer is that any reform that will be acceptable to the system's precariously balanced dependents will leave its structure and incentives untouched.

"Innovations" and "solutions" will necessarily be superficial and for show because that preserves a system that has reached its limits, a system defined by choiceless choices that create an illusion of autonomy: Democrat / Republican, Apple / Android, a choiceless healthcare system, a choiceless higher education system, and so on.

Given its limits, the entire system has only one option: decline to the point that a seemingly modest crisis disrupts the last shreds of coherence in a system that is now dependent on the destabilizing expediencies of ever-expanding borrowing and credit-asset bubbles, and the parodies, PR, delusions and fantasies of The Big Con. The inevitable result is the system collapses under its own weight of self-serving sclerosis and artifice.

The incentives are to repeat what everyone wants to hear, which is the system is working fine and is sustainable because technology and finance will fix everything without changing anything. This describes a system that has reached its limits.

items.title: Alina Habba Fired From $50M Gig After Trump Outburst
items.content_text:
Alina Habba Fired From $50M Gig After Trump Outburst

Alina Habba, the former Trump lawyer and New Jersey US attorney who now goes by Alina Habba Mildon, has been fired from the general counsel job that guaranteed her more than $50 million over four years, cut loose by a company set up by the daughter of a billionaire banker President Trump pardoned in January. Concord Partners, the Herrera family's Florida firm, ended her contract in a Nov. 4 letter citing a "failure to perform duties," The New York Times reported Tuesday.

The firing came four days after Trump turned on her in public. She still walks away with $14.5 million: about $6.5 million in salary collected since January and an $8 million signing bonus, according to the Times' reporter on the story.

NEWS: Alina Habba's $50 million contract was terminated last week.

Company fired her for "failure to perform duties." She will keep $6.5 mil in salary and $8 mil signing bonus.

The firing came days after The Times reporting prompted a Trump outburst.https://t.co/TLqGda12Og

— Tyler Pager (@tylerpager) November 10, 2026

A person close to the Herrera family told the Times that her focus drifted from Concord after she began dating Turhan Mildon, the 25-year-old Turkish investor she married in September. Habba Mildon declined to comment on the firing, and a person close to her said she intends to take legal action. Representatives for the family also declined to comment.

Asked about the deal by reporters at a Halloween party at Mar-a-Lago on Oct. 31, Trump said he had told her he didn't want her paid, as we reported at the time. "She used her relationship to do that and it was far too much," he said. "I thought it was totally obnoxious and outrageous and it's not acceptable. Not acceptable at all." Asked whether she should donate to his presidential library, he answered, "No, not her."

"I thought it was totally obnoxious and outrageous." 💰
Asked Oct. 31 about former lawyer Alina Habba Mildon's reported $50 million-plus contract, the President said "I don't want her paid."#Trump #AlinaHabba #CapitolClips 
Source: The White House, public domain pic.twitter.com/hRh6nvDOdV

— Capitol Clips (@CapitolClipps) November 4, 2026

The deal itself surfaced in an Oct. 20 Times investigation. Isabela Herrera, the 27-year-old daughter of Venezuelan banker Julio Herrera Velutini, registered Concord Partners in Florida in late October 2025, and Habba finalized a $10 million-a-year contract with it days later, while she was still New Jersey's acting US attorney. The company has no public profile, and what it does is unclear. Isabela Herrera has also given $3.5 million to a pro-Trump super PAC.

Habba resigned as US attorney on Dec. 8 after the courts ruled she was serving unlawfully, as we reported when an appeals court ruled against her and when she stepped down. The same day she became a senior adviser to Attorney General Pam Bondi as a special government employee, a status that allows outside work, and she started at Concord on Jan. 1 while still holding the Justice Department post.

Herrera had been charged in 2022 with a scheme to bribe then-Puerto Rico Gov. Wanda Vázquez into removing a regulator who was investigating his bank, and he pleaded guilty in August 2025 to a single misdemeanor campaign finance charge. Weeks after Habba went to work for his daughter's company, Trump signed "a full and unconditional pardon" for him in the case, according to the clemency grant posted by the Justice Department. Vázquez was pardoned at the same time.

Habba Mildon has said she was never paid for a pardon and did no work toward one, calling any suggestion that her employment had anything to do with it "false and defamatory." The Justice Department has said she never discussed a pardon with anyone, and a White House official has said the family's donations had nothing to do with it.

Her new husband's money is the subject of a separate fight. As we reported on Nov. 1, Habba told Trump in the Oval Office that Richard Grenell never delivered roughly $5.6 million of a $17.6 million payment Mildon wired at his direction, a claim Grenell denies. White House counsel Will Scharf has been told to look into it. Habba Mildon now faces both fights at once: a possible lawsuit against the family that hired her, and a White House review of her husband's money.

Iran Hawk Bessent Now Lives Behind A Military Gate As Threats Reach 'More Than Advanced Stage'

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has moved out of his Washington-area home and onto a US military base because of Iranian threats against him, the New York Times reported Tuesday.

Three people told the Times that US officials concluded in recent weeks that Iranian plotting against current and former American officials had reached a more advanced stage, based in part on intelligence about threats to Bessent himself.

A senior administration official told Fox News the threats against Bessent's life had reached "more than an advanced stage," and declined to say when he moved.

BREAKING: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has moved to a military base after Iranian threats against his life reached "more than an advanced stage," a senior administration official tells Fox News Digital.

The official says the threats prompted Bessent and his family to make... pic.twitter.com/Ei25bRHwRE

— Fox News (@FoxNews) November 11, 2026

The Treasury Department, confirming the move, said Bessent "will not be deterred by the Iranian regime's threats" and remains committed to the pressure campaign against Tehran.

Bessent has run Operation Economic Outcast since Aug. 24, a campaign he says is meant "to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone." Launching it, he declared: "America is no longer managing the Iranian threat. We are ending it."

In September, Treasury sanctioned all of Iran's remaining airlines, with Bessent warning anyone still doing business with them: "You are at risk of being cut off from the global financial system." On Nov. 4, a day after Republicans were crushed in midterms widely seen as a referendum on the Iran war, he announced another round, as we reported: "As we have said many times, under Operation Economic Outcast, you are either with us or against us."

Last week, as we noted, MEMRI flagged an Iranian video that calls Bessent "Captain Corruptor" and warns that he "has booked himself a first class ticket to Hell and his ride will soon arrive at his door."

In a memo to Secretary of State Marco Rubio last month, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned that "Iran has substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel" and that "the lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against U.S. citizens have reached advanced stages" in the Middle East and certain other countries.

Bessent and Rubio rode a decoy Air Force One out of Ankara after the NATO summit in July while Trump secretly switched planes. A senior administration official told ABC News that Trump's switch was driven by intelligence that an Iranian terror cell had slipped into Turkey with a shoulder-fired missile.

items.title: New Car Prices Top $51,000, Monthly Payments At Record. What Could Possibly Go Wrong?
items.content_text:
New Car Prices Top $51,000, Monthly Payments At Record. What Could Possibly Go Wrong?

The average price of a new vehicle in the US has climbed to a record $51,109, according to a new Cox Automotive report citing Kelley Blue Book data. Combined with new-car loan rates near their highest levels since the mid-2000s, record sticker prices are putting vehicle ownership increasingly out of reach for many working-class folks, even before insurance, fuel and maintenance costs are factored in.

Cox said average new-car prices in October rose 2.1% from the same month one year ago to $51,109, outpacing overall inflation. The average manufacturer's suggested retail price (MSRP) also climbed 2.4% year over year to $52,933.

"A big part of the reason for the record-high average comes down to what Americans are buying. Shoppers continue to gravitate toward larger, more expensive vehicles, particularly mid-size SUVs and full-size pickup trucks," automotive news outlet Motor1 said.

Automotive research firm Edmunds wrote in its Q3 report last month that the average new-car monthly payment reached $787, a record high, while average used-car monthly payments were around $582.

Highlights from the Edmunds report:

  • Average new-car monthly payment: $787, a record, versus $777 in Q2 and $756 a year earlier.
  • Average used-car monthly payment: $582, versus $566 a year earlier.
  • 21.2% of financed new-car buyers committed to payments of $1,000 or more per month.
  • 25.5% took out loans lasting 84 months or longer, another record.
  • The average amount financed for a new car reached $44,664, with an average 7% APR.

"What we're seeing in the data is a remarkable display of consumer resilience against a very stretched financing landscape," said Jessica Caldwell, Edmunds' head of insights.

Caldwell explained, "Even as monthly payments hit record highs, loan terms stretch to historic lengths, and four-figure monthly payments become more common, buyer demand for new vehicles hasn't dropped off. Instead of sitting on the sidelines, consumers are adapting: They're allocating more of their household budgets to their vehicles, stretching out their loan terms, and becoming more proactive about shopping around for financing to find ways to make the numbers work."

What could possibly go wrong? Well...

  • Nearly 3 In 10 New-Car Trade-Ins Are Underwater, Edmunds Finds
  • While Subprime Auto Loans Default, Their Bonds Somehow Keep Performing

The next trend in the auto space will be bare-bones vehicles without all the bells and whistles. 

Toyota has recognized this emerging trend and will begin producing affordable mini trucks at its Indiana plant in the second half of 2027 (read here).

items.title: 'Run Socialists In Every Primary': Emboldened DSA Turns Its Guns On Fellow Democrats
items.content_text:
'Run Socialists In Every Primary': Emboldened DSA Turns Its Guns On Fellow Democrats

Authored by Jake Altman via City Journal,

Last week's historic midterm results have emboldened not just the Democratic Party but also the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA). The organization expanded its House caucus from two to eight and added a key ally, Abdul El-Sayed, to the Senate. Adding local wins and ballot initiatives, the group touted "50 DSA victories" overall.

Over 50 DSA victories tonight prove socialism can win in the U.S. 

Workers deserve more and a reality where all of us live with dignity and hope is closer than we think.

The job's not done, though. Tomorrow, we continue organizing, fighting, and winning for the working class!

— DSA (@DemSocialists) November 4, 2026

Yet while hopes are running high, the size of the Democratic majority and the DSA's own fractious internal culture pose significant challenges to the organization's ability to capitalize long term. The DSA will face pushback from moderates within the Democratic Party. Moreover, as the organization garners greater public recognition and scrutiny, it risks becoming a political liability for allies - particularly if it cannot keep its most extreme wing in check.

The midterm results reinforced the DSA's conviction that its candidates can win anywhere. Jacobin staff writer Branko Marcetic's analysis declared that the election "finally proved left policies and rhetoric are not the electoral liability Democratic voters have been told for decades it is."

With this conclusion in mind, the DSA is shifting its focus toward intra-party primary battles ahead of 2028. Capturing the DSA's aggressive mood, leftist streamer Hasan Piker asserted, "We should have f***ing ran socialists in every f***ing primary, dude." Meantime, communication co-chair Aron Ali-McClory wrote, "at a base line, the socialist presence in Congress will soar to heights unseen in over a century. We are contesting in places that've been written off for decades. It's only a beginning, but let the light in!"

🚨 Hasan Piker Laments the DSA's Missed Opportunity to Flood Democratic Primaries With Communists

"We should have fucking ran socialists in every fucking primary, dude."

"We should have been running straight communists in some of these blue districts, and running the moderate... pic.twitter.com/z0iAS6YmF6

— Stu Smith (@thestustustudio) November 4, 2026

Ali-McClory's statement, amplified by the DSA's official account, highlights the triumphalist atmosphere within the organization. DSA-ers seem to believe that full-throated socialism - not sober Danish-style social democracy - is asserting itself in American politics.

The next step is to bring the fight to the rest of the Democratic Party. Piker made clear during his election night stream that Hillary Scholten - a Michigan Democrat who did not endorse DSA ally El-Sayed - is a top target for a 2028 primary challenge. Given its recent momentum, the DSA seems eager to settle scores with intra-party rivals.

At the same time, however, signs of awareness are emerging within DSA that its most radical factions and the public demands they place on elected members could backfire in a less favorable political climate, jeopardizing recent electoral gains and damaging the broader socialist project.

Tensions between the hardcore activist base and elected officials, who must navigate the realities of governance and reelection, are already apparent. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, for example, has resisted pressure from hardliners to adopt policies that could hurt him politically, such as demands that he fire Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch. Just last month, far-left activists targeted Mamdani for mob treatment. Fortunately for the mayor, New York City's finest were on hand to protect him.

Marcetic's postelection analysis in Jacobin captured the DSA's central dilemma: Should it demand strict ideological discipline from its elected officials, or grant them tactical flexibility? Reflecting on the Senate campaign in Florida, Marcetic noted, "[Angie Nixon's] strong showing, along with the success of other left-wing candidates who similarly moderated or eschewed contemporary left orthodoxy on some issues, points to the benefits of DSA candidates having the flexibility to tailor campaigns to local electorates."

The organization is deeply divided on the flexibility issue. DSA leadership has shown some capacity to rein in provocative moves, as seen in a narrow vote against revoking a local chapter's endorsement of Nithya Raman - now mayor-elect of Los Angeles. The vote was split 14 to 13, and Bread and Roses, the caucus holding the DSA's center ground, divided its votes on the question.

With the national board so evenly split, the upcoming 2027 DSA convention promises to be pivotal, as hardline factions continue pushing for stringent ideological tests at a time when the DSA is expected to field a presidential contender.

Expect growing friction both within the DSA and within the Democratic Party as internal tensions and the illusion of unity give way under the pressures of public scrutiny and political necessity.

items.title: Trump Picks Palantir's Security Chief To Run CISA
items.content_text:
Trump Picks Palantir's Security Chief To Run CISA

Authored by Owen Evans via The Epoch Times,

The White House said on Monday it nominated Michael LoSapio to lead America's premier cyber defense agency. If confirmed by the Senate, LoSapio will take over from the Department of Homeland Security's Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) acting director, Nick Andersen.

CISA, which leads the national effort to understand, manage, and reduce risk to cyber and physical infrastructure, has lacked a Senate-confirmed leader for almost 22 months, since Jen Easterly resigned in January 2025.

LoSapio's nomination comes after large-scale breaches at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and the FBI were disclosed in the past few months.

According to his LinkedIn profile, he has served as Palantir's chief information security officer (CISO) since September 2024. Since 2017, he has led the company's infrastructure and network security group.

President Donald Trump nominated Sean Plankey as CISA chief in March 2025. However, Plankey withdrew his name from Senate consideration in April this year.

When Democrats take control of both legislative chambers, including the Senate, in January, they can block or delay Trump nominees. CISA has lost some staff since Trump returned to office.

For example, according to a September report from the federal watchdog Government Accountability Office, CISA's active personnel dedicated to chemical sector activities declined from 214 to 52 in fiscal year 2024-25. Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (D-Va.), a member of the House Committee on Homeland Security Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection, claimed on Sept. 21 that one-third of CISA has been "hollowed out." The Epoch Times has not independently verified these claims. In July, DHS probed a cyber breach in an unclassified legacy information-sharing system used to exchange sensitive data with law enforcement partners.

The breach affected the Homeland Security Information Network (HSIN), which oversees sharing sensitive but unclassified information with foreign law enforcement, local authorities, and other organizations.

The incident is thought to have occurred sometime between late May and early June.

An internal database with personal information identifying more than 41,000 employees at the DHS, including undercover immigration officers, was hacked by activists and published online, the group claimed on Oct. 28.

The FBI also recently arrested a suspect linked to ShinyHunters, the cybercriminal group suspected of being responsible for the recent breach of the bureau's jobs website.

On Sept. 22, a message on the FBI website FBIJobs.gov said it was "unavailable." The FBI's Special Agent Applicant Portal showed the same message.

"This is the latest arrest this FBI has made in a matter of days involving this network, as we work non-stop to dismantle the group, pursue new leads and evidence, and act quickly," FBI Director Kash Patel said in an Oct. 9 post on X.

Patel said the FBI's jobs website was hacked through "a platform managed by a third-party vendor."

Democrats have raised concerns about Palantir Technologies over the company's federal contracts and data-handling practices.

In June 2025, 10 members of Congress, including Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), accused the company of "enabling violations of human rights" and promised a full investigation into both Palantir and the Trump administration.

"We are not building, we have not been asked to build, and we're not in contract to build any kind of federal master list or master database across different agencies," Courtney Bowman, Palantir's global director of privacy and civil liberties engineering, told The Epoch Times at the time.

"Each of those contracts are separate and fulfill specific mandates that are scoped and bound by congressional authorities and other laws."

On Monday, former Democratic Sen. Jon Tester (D-Mont.) said Palantir had hired him.

"My agreement with Palantir is advisory in nature, it is not lobbying," Tester told NPR in an interview on Nov. 9.

"Perception is reality in Washington, D.C., and in politics in general. But the fact is, I think Palantir has got a good story to tell, and they need to tell it. And hopefully folks will be receptive to it."

items.title: Peltola's Alaska Lead Now Tops Every 'Decoy Dan' Vote... Trump's Math Just Broke
items.content_text:
Peltola's Alaska Lead Now Tops Every 'Decoy Dan' Vote... Trump's Math Just Broke

Democrat Mary Peltola's lead over Sen. Dan Sullivan (R-Alaska) has grown past the vote total of the second Dan Sullivan on the ballot, so even handing the senator every vote cast for the man Republicans call "Decoy Dan" would no longer put him ahead.

After the Alaska Division of Elections' Nov. 10 update, which covers 401 of the state's 403 precincts, Peltola has 118,926 first-choice votes, or 49%, to Sullivan's 114,676, or 47.2%. Her margin of 4,250 is up from 2,517 a day earlier and from 637 last week, when the count stood at 102,962 to 102,325.

Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., the retired Petersburg schoolteacher whose candidacy is under state and federal investigation, has 4,027 votes. Add all of them to the senator's 114,676 and he reaches 118,703: still 223 votes behind Peltola.

"Dan Sullivan PLUS Dan Sullivan wins the Alaska Election by thousands of votes," President Trump wrote on Truth Social at 7:36 a.m. Eastern on Tuesday. "All votes going to the Fake Dan Sullivan, which was done solely for the purpose of fraud and confusion, should immediately be given to the Real Dan Sullivan (Senator!)" Trump called it a "Rigged Election." Later that day the new ballot drop put Peltola past the combined total.

Trump's post went one step further: "Likewise the votes of the second fraudulent candidate, also put up by the Dems." That is Gerald Heikes, the Palmer Republican in third with 5,318 votes. Stack his total on top as well and Sullivan would lead by 5,095. 

Without Heikes, the "Dan PLUS Dan" sum no longer works.

If no one tops 50%, the Division of Elections doesn't add candidates together; it runs its ranked-choice tabulation on Nov. 18. The last-place candidate is eliminated, and each of those ballots moves to the voter's next choice still in the race, round after round, until someone has a majority of the ballots left. A vote moves to the senator only if that voter ranked him.

The early data on those rankings favors Peltola. In the cast vote record the state released on Nov. 4, covering about 204,000 scanned ballots, only about 16% of Petersburg Sullivan's voters ranked the senator second, while a little over a quarter ranked Peltola second, according to an analysis by Alaska Public Media. About half of Heikes' voters ranked the senator anywhere on their ballots. Nearly 30,000 Peltola voters ranked the Petersburg Sullivan second.

On those shares, the second Sullivan's 4,027 votes would give the senator about 640 and Peltola about 1,000. Heikes' 5,318 would give the senator about 2,660 more if every one of those rankings reached him. That nets Sullivan roughly 2,300 votes, a little over half the 4,250 he trails by. The cast vote record left out rural precincts that hand-count Election Day ballots, as well as the early and absentee ballots still being counted, so the shares could shift.

Sullivan's campaign made the opposite case in a Nov. 5 memo, when Peltola led by 637: "If the ranked choice voting tabulation took place today of the votes that we have in hand right now, Senator Dan Sullivan would defeat Mary Peltola," it said, calling the race "the biggest election cheating scandal in the history of Alaska." Peltola's campaign called that "fictitious."

"Alaskans are fed up with high costs and corruption stemming from DC, and they have made their voices heard: after every vote is counted, it is clear that Mary Peltola will be elected Alaska's next United States Senator," Cheryl Bruce, Peltola's campaign manager, said in a Nov. 10 statement.

Yesterday's ballot drop delivered positive results, and we expect more updates shortly.

Our thorough counting process is something to appreciate. It means every ballot gets counted and every voice gets heard. That's how the system is supposed to work.https://t.co/mbOkD1abTS

— Mary Peltola (@MaryPeltola) November 11, 2026

Gov. Mike Dunleavy said in a Sunday interview that big ballot drops are expected on Friday, Nov. 13, and on Wednesday, Nov. 18, the day of the ranked-choice count. The results are set to be certified Nov. 25. Peltola's campaign has also sued the state over absentee ballots it rejected.

The second Sullivan has hung over the race since the New York Times reported on Oct. 28 that operatives around Peltola's campaign spent months hunting for Alaskans named Dan Sullivan to put on the ballot. Peltola's campaign denies recruiting anyone. Dunleavy ordered a criminal investigation the next day, a federal judge threw out the Justice Department's bid to block certification if Sullivan lost, and the federal probe has now reached Democratic lawyer Marc Elias, according to Just the News.

Democrats and the independents who caucus with them already have at least 54 Senate seats in the next Congress to the Republicans' 44, with Alaska and Mississippi uncalled. In Mississippi, Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith trails Democrat Scott Colom by 2,990 votes, and if both seats fall, Democrats would hold 56.

items.title: RFK Jr. Says Big Developments Coming In Wake Of Midterms
items.content_text:
RFK Jr. Says Big Developments Coming In Wake Of Midterms

Authored by Zachary Stieber via The Epoch Times,

Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said Nov. 9 that multiple recent changes are paving the way for major reforms he has been unable to enact in his nearly two years as the nation's top health official.

Kennedy told supporters at an event in Washington that key actions, such as updating the food pyramid and removing mercury from dental fillings on Indian reservations, were enacted with White House support, including backing from Susie Wiles, who was White House chief of staff until several days ago.

However, he said, other goals have not yet been implemented.

"There were things that we didn't get done, and that was very frustrating to me," he said. "And they are very, very important things."

Stephen Miller, the longtime aide to President Donald Trump and the new chief of staff, met with Kennedy before the midterm elections and told Kennedy that after the midterms, he would put Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) initiatives at the top of his priority list, according to Kennedy.

The health secretary also said that he went to Miller's house for dinner on Nov. 1, and Miller's wife told guests that they had no idea how passionate Miller is on MAHA.

Miller said during a 2025 MAHA event that his wife was a MAHA mom and he had been shocked to learn of all the toxins children are exposed to, including toxins in food and the environment.

"What Secretary Kennedy has done at the direction and leadership of President Trump is for the first time in American history, the full power and authority of the federal government is being used to identify and solve the chronic disease epidemic, and not to cover it up," Miller said at the time.

Kennedy's new comments came after a former adviser, Calley Means, accused Wiles and other White House officials of stymying attempts by MAHA-aligned officials to implement reforms such as compelling companies to make food healthier and working with them to do so. The White House said that the Trump administration does not allow outside groups to influence policy decisions.

They also followed Democrats flipping the Senate and multiple senators or senator-elects calling for the removal of Kennedy from office over allegations that he has mishandled health-related efforts and promoted misinformation on vaccines.

"Secretary Kennedy has delivered the most sweeping public health reforms in modern history," a spokesperson for the Department of Health and Human Services told news outlets in a statement. "He will continue to put prevention at the center of health care to end the chronic disease epidemic and Make America Healthy Again. Threats of impeachment will not distract him from delivering for the American people."

Kennedy said on Monday that he has faced obstacles from several areas, including Republican senators.

"Every time I try to do something robust, I would get calls saying, 'If you do that, we're not going to confirm your appointees,'" he recounted.

Kennedy has faced public opposition from multiple senators, including Senate Health Committee Chairman Bill Cassidy (R-La.), who lost in a primary to Sen.-elect Julia Letlow (R-La.).

"The Senate no longer has any leverage over me, and that's a big deal," Kennedy said. "And then we have Steve Miller in, who's a friend of our movement, and I don't think anything is going to get in our way now."

Kennedy declined to list specific developments that are being targeted.

"There's a lot of press here, and I don't want to unveil our strategies," he said.

Kennedy referenced a post on X in which he said it was time to "unleash the Kraken" following Trump announcing Miller as the new chief of staff.

"That's what we're about to do," he said on Monday.

Next to me, Stephen Miller is the strongest MAHA supporter in the administration. It's time to unleash the Kraken. https://t.co/adYAkyjkJb

— Secretary Kennedy (@SecKennedy) November 6, 2026

items.title: 假如地球没有诞生生命？
items.content_text: 假如地球没有诞生生命，它会变成什么模样？华盛顿大学团队进行了计算机模拟，他们将生命的因素彻底抽离，但完整保留了地核、地函、大气、海洋以及太阳辐射等 19 项关键物理变数，模拟这颗没有生命的地球从 45 亿年前诞生至今、乃至未来 5 亿年的演化史。在长达数十亿年的岁月里，这颗死寂的地球除了因为没有植物进行光合作用而极度缺乏氧气外，其地表温度与液态水量竟然与我们今天的真实地球相差无几。在天文学的定义中，宜居的核心标准并非空气中是否有氧气，而是地表能否维持液态水。模拟显示，即使没有生物参与，地球本身的碳酸盐-矽酸盐循环便足以扛起调节气候的重任。当太阳在数十亿年间逐渐变亮变热时，岩石风化、火山喷气与海洋化学反应所形成的机制，能自动平衡大气中的二氧化碳浓度，将地表温度死死锁定在宜居范围内。研究暗示了行星的宜居性与生命的存在在某种程度上是可以分开的。

items.content_text: 苹果突然宣布关闭其支持社区 Support Community：它将于 2026 年 11 月 20 日永久关闭，即日起进入只读模式，用户无法再发新帖。想要获得帮助的苹果用户可访问 Apple Support 网站，但他们将无法互相交流。苹果支持社区创建于 1998 年，是一个用户互相交流和讨论问题的论坛，它的关闭标志着三十年积累的建议、故障排查经验以及未获解答问题都戛然而止，苹果未说明支持社区存档是否还能访问。

items.title: 黑猩猩后天习得部分叫声
items.content_text: 长期以来，人们认为野生黑猩猩的发声完全由遗传决定，无需学习。发表于 PNAS 期刊上的一项研究挑战了这一观点，首次发现了野生黑猩猩中存在任意性、习得性发声惯例的证据。该发现缩小了黑猩猩交流与人类交流之间的差距。词语在人类语言中具有任意性和习得性。这里的任意性指一个词语在不同背景或领域里含义可能完全不同。词语在使用过程中的任意性，最终形成了因社群而异的语言惯例。一个人之所以遵循这些惯例，是因为同伴都这样做；如果同伴改变了用法，个体也就会遵循这些改变。研究人员分析了野生黑猩猩和圈养黑猩猩都会发出的嘟噜声的使用情况。研究涵盖了91只年龄在0到55岁的黑猩猩，其中一部是科特迪瓦塔伊国家公园的野生黑猩猩，另一部是塞拉利昂塔库加马黑猩猩保护区中由与同龄伙伴一起长大的孤儿黑猩猩。分析结果表明，野生黑猩猩只在相互梳理毛发时才使用这种叫声，而保护区里的孤儿黑猩猩则在多种社交互动中使用它。这表明该叫声的用法需要习得，而非遗传决定的。为了进一步证明该结论，研究人员在第二阶段的实验中，将一只成年黑猩猩引入其中一个孤儿黑猩猩群体。结果随着时间推移，该群体使用嘟噜声的方式明显趋于一致，并向成年黑猩猩的用法靠拢。这表明幼年黑猩猩会像人类一样，向年长者学习叫声的功能。上述发现表明，黑猩猩的声音交流比此前认为的更接近人类。

items.title: 刚果埃博拉病例突破 1.1 万例
items.content_text: 刚果政府周三宣布该国的埃博拉病例突破 1.1 万例达到 11,042 例，有 5,387 人死亡，这是刚果至今最致命的埃博拉疫情，感染者中近半数死亡。这场疫情已成为有记录以来扩散速度最快的埃博拉病毒爆发，其规模有可能超过 2014-2016 年席卷西非的埃博拉疫情——该波疫情有逾 1.1 万人死亡。这起疫情的病毒是罕见的 Bundibugyo 毒株，目前没有针对该毒株的获批疫苗或疗法。

items.title: AI 生成的代码并不可靠
items.content_text: 一位 100% 依赖 AI 生成代码的资深开发者认为 AI 生成的代码库无法满足高可用、高扩展性 SaaS 应用的需求。原因包括：AI 写的测试过于简单，无法覆盖真正重要的使用场景；AI 写的代码过于复杂，经常引入两三个辅助方法，实际上一个就够了，这种复杂性增加了理解代码或进行调试的难度；人类程序员难以理解 AI 生成的代码库，一家企业依赖 AI 生成代码库的时间越长，真正理解代码库的程序员就越少；AI 产出速度太快，无法维持高质量标准，人工审核的时间越来越短，从而会造成长期的技术债务。AI 生成的代码库会导致更多故障，而故障修复的时间会越来越长。

items.title: CERN 如何为 LHC 研发下一代磁体
items.content_text: CERN 的大强子对撞机（LHC）利用极其强大的磁体，使粒子接近光速发生碰撞，将粒子撞碎成更小的组成部分以供研究。当前状态下的 LHC 每秒能让约 60 个粒子发生碰撞，碰撞频率高达每秒 4000 万次。这一能力已经促成了本世纪粒子物理学领域一些最重要的发现。CERN 的科学家并没有止步。他们正对 LHC 进行升级，为计划于 2030  年之后开始的实验做准备。新一代粒子对撞机被称为高亮度大型强子对撞机（High-Luminosity LHC 或 HL-LHC），高亮度指的是粒子碰撞数量的增加。CERN 的目标是每次实验将碰撞涉及的粒子数量提高到 140-200 个，增加观测到罕见粒子或特殊物理现象的机会。为实现这一目标，对撞机需要配备体积极其紧凑、性能优异的磁体。目前对撞机使用的偶极磁体内部装有由铌钛合金（NbTi）制成的线圈，其磁场强度可达到 8.3 特斯拉。这一强度约为地球磁场的 16.6 万倍。这已经是铌钛线圈所能达到的磁场强度上限。为制造 HL-LHC 使用四极磁体，科学家正在研发由铌锡化合物（Nb₃Sn）制成的线圈，其磁场强度将接近 12 特斯拉。

items.title: 猫围着你叫是叫你去解决问题
items.content_text: 当猫不停喵喵声时，它们不只是表达对世界的不满，更多是刻意引起你的注意，希望你能去解决问题。没留意到也没关系，毕竟人类向来以难以理解猫想要表达什么而著称。一项新研究发现，在猫的生活中，人类扮演着问题解决者的角色。巴西的研究人员针对 38 只宠物猫调查了人类主人在场和不在场时的行为。结果显示，人类铲屎官在场时，猫发出喵喵叫的次数增至四倍。结果表明，喵喵叫确实在人猫互动中起到了沟通交流的作用。在实验中，研究人员设计了一个有孔的食物盒子，猫能闻到食物气味但无法接触到里面的食物。当人类在场时，猫总共发出了 86 次叫声；而当猫独自待着时，叫声仅有 20 次。猫确实是在通过叫声表达对所处困境的不满。

items.title: 英伟达股价 2 天暴跌 10%
items.content_text: 英伟达股价两天暴跌 10%。市场担忧该公司对黄仁勋的高度依赖，围绕“关键人物风险”的警惕情绪令相关股票走势分化。英伟达缺乏继任者并非始于今日。黄仁勋自公司创立以来已领导企业 30 多年，且不设董事长职务的治理结构。这对于如此规模的美国大型企业实属罕见。美国调查公司伯恩斯坦研究公司的 Stacy Rasgon 指出：“英伟达不是一家普通公司。黄仁勋也不是一位普通 CEO”。 分析师预测，如果英伟达出现 CEO 更迭，股价可能下跌 25%-30%。SpaceX、特斯拉的 CEO 马斯克以及 Meta 的 CEO 扎克伯格同样面临关键人物风险。SpaceX 的招股说明书中写道，“无法保证能够及时找到（马斯克的）继任者，甚至不知能否找到”。

items.title: Michael John Harrison 成为首位获得布克奖的科幻作家
items.content_text: 81 岁的哈里森（Michael John Harrison）成为首位获得布克奖的科幻作家，也是获得布克奖的最年长作家。他的获奖作品是末日小说《The End of Everything》，故事设定在一场无人能正确解释的灾难后数十年，地点是英国的肯特郡海岸，讲诉了 Phillip Tennent 和年迈的姑姑 Marnie 在神秘的 iGhetti 带来的威胁下艰难求生。Ghetti 是一种庞大且能不断变形的生物，其起源和意图未给出说明。哈里森的创作生涯长达六十年，其年龄超过了 2019 年的布克奖得主 Margaret Atwood——时年 79 岁。布克奖基金会 CEO Gaby Wood 表示，尽管此前已有不少获奖者涉足过科幻文学，但哈里森是第一位真正来自科幻界的布克奖得主。

items.title: AMD 公布 Zen 6 CPU 细节
items.content_text: AMD 披露了 Zen 6 CPU 家族的细节。从表面看，Zen 6 是 Zen 5 的自然演进，核心扩展了乱序执行结构以及其它方面的迭代改进。但深入内部会发现 AMD 对核心的多个方面进行了重构，其改进类似从 Zen 1 到 Zen 2。 Zen 6 分支预测错误开销从 Zen 5 的 3.5-4 纳秒缩短到了 3-3.5 纳秒，降低了分支预测错误延迟。Zen 6 能在 L1 指令缓存内实现每周期处理 2 个分支，指令足迹超出 L1 缓存容量后会降至每周期处理 1 个分支，Zen 6 主要提升了分支目标缓冲器（BTB）的速度而非容量。Zen 6 的分支预测单元精确度接近 Zen 5，执行速度则更快。Zen 5 单线程只能使用一个解码集群，而 Zen 6 提升到了单线程能使用两个解码集群。Zen 6 在整数运算上恢复了 Zen 4 的 NOP（空操作）配对机制，每时钟周期最多可处理 16 个 NOP，配备相同的 6 个算术逻辑单元 Zen 6 每时钟周期可完成 5.96 次 64 位加法运算而 Zen 5 为 5.25 次。AMD 将整数乘法单元的数量从 3 个减少到了 2 个，理由是 3 个整数乘法单元带来的性能提升不足以抵消占用的芯片面积成本。Zen 5 的经典核心（Classic cores）与高密度核心（Dense cores）在架构上几乎完全相同，区别在于单个 CCD 内的核心数量以及每个核心所分配的 L3 缓存大小。但 Zen 6 家族发生了变化。AMD 对 Zen 6 与 Zen 6c 进行了架构的差异性设计，Zen 6c 部分乱序执行结构的容量更大，能同时处理更多的指令，更好应对较高的延迟。Zen 6 优化了高频，而 Zen 6c 能更好容忍较高的内存延迟。Zen 6 和 Zen 6c 分别采用 12 核和 32 核的 CCD 设计，每个核心均配备 4 MB 的 L3 缓存。12 核 CCD 拥有 48 MB 的 L3 缓存，32 核 CCD 拥有 128 MB。L3 缓存延迟从 Zen 5 的约 47 个周期增加到 Zen 6 的 55 个周期和 Zen 6c 的 66 个周期，原因可能是缓存容量的增大以及网格互连节点数量的增加。Zen 6 通过更高的时钟频率抵消了延迟增幅，Zen 6c 则因为低时钟频率以及更大的 CCX 显著增加了延迟。AMD 的测试显示 zen 6 整数运算提升 14% 浮点提升 11%，Zen 6c ipc 提升 20%。

items.title: 微软宣布 .NET 11
items.content_text: 微软宣布了 .NET 11。该版本是标准支持版本 STS，提供两年支持，上个版本 .NET 10 则是长期支持版本 LTS。.NET 11 改进 C# 15、ASP.NET Core、.NET MAUI 以及 Windows，缩短了应用构建时间，主要变化包括：C# 15 引入了联合类型和封闭类层次结构；Native AOT CLI；ASP.NET Core 支持异步验证和 OpenAPI 3.2，以及 Blazor 和 SignalR 应用的新功能；等等。

items.title: 2026 年全球化石燃料碳排放量预计下降 0.4%
items.content_text: 根据 Global Carbon Project 发表的报告《2026 Global Carbon Budget》，因太阳能风能扩张以及冲突导致的石油供应问题，2026 年全球化石燃料碳排放量预计下降 0.4%。今年全球化石燃料二氧化碳（CO2）排放量预计为 382 亿吨，其中石油相关排放量预计下降 1.9%。尽管全球能源需求持续增长，但三分之二增量已被太阳能、风能以及电动汽车的发展所抵消或满足。报告同时指出清洁能源的增长速度尚不足以促使全球化石燃料二氧化碳排放量持续下降。由于土地利用变化（如森林砍伐）导致今年的总排放量略有增加，2026 年全球二氧化碳排放总量预计达到 433 亿吨，高于去年的 428 亿吨。报告预计 2026 年中国的排放量将下降 0.9%，印度碳排放量将增长 4.4%，欧盟将下降 1.5%，日本量将下降 1%。

items.title: 波士顿动力为其人形机器人加入了轮子
items.content_text: 波士顿动力通过官方 YouTube 频道公布了一则新视频，展示了其人形机器人 Atlas 改用轮子在地面上移动。视频展示了 Atlas 能通过足部的轮子用脚尖旋转，以及做出其它高强度的动作。Atlas 能在平坦地面上的快速滚动与应对障碍物或不规则地面的关节式腿部运动之间实现平滑切换。Atlas 项目控制工程师 Andy Wu 称，系统在模拟环境中进行了训练，在模拟环境中学会所有动作后能在现实世界中以高准确度执行出来。Atlas 转换到移动模式仅需一个定制的适配器，就能将现有的滑板车轮毂安装到 Atlas 原有的踝关节执行器上。

items.title: 中国 Android 厂商开始要求开发者身份验证
items.content_text: Google 从今年 9 月起要求验证所有 Android 应用开发者的身份，未经身份验证的开发者的应用未来将无法在 Android 设备上安装（sideload）。Google 官方博客声称它是出于安全理由要求验证开发者身份，理由是其分析显示来自第三方源的恶意应用数量是 Google Play 的 90 多倍。现在，中国主要 Android 厂商也启动了开发者身份验证：OPPO、vivo、小米、荣耀推出 Android 侧载应用开发者身份验证（Android Developer Verification，简称 ADV），支持各方验证结果互认。ADV 旨在建立开发者与其应用之间的可信关联，为用户识别应用来源、判断应用是否安全提供依据。

items.title: 生成式 AI 过度美化现实
items.content_text: 生成式 AI 如 ChatGPT 正融入日常生活，成为人们获取信息和辅助决策的重要工具。然而大模型中嵌入的错误信息和偏见引发了一系列伦理方面的担忧。以往的研究已揭示出 AI 在涉及人类特征的内容上存在偏见，例如肤色、性别以及地理文化背景等。为减轻文本生成图像（Text-to-Image）生成式模型中的偏见，OpenAI 等公司引入了提示词修订（Prompt Revision）机制。一种隐性的处理过程，即通过重写用户输入的提示词，添加更多细节，例如要求图像中呈现不同性别和肤色的人物，从而促进图像的多样性。然而重写用户提示词也可能引入其他偏见，在用户不知情下改变其原本的意图。发表在《Technology in Society》上的一项研究以集约化畜牧业（Intensive Livestock Farming）为例，首次提供证据表明，OpenAI 的文本生成图像模型 DALL-E 3 会通过提示词修订机制，抹去具有争议性议题的真实面貌。DALL-E 3 表现出一种明显的偏见，即倾向于将畜牧业浪漫化、美化。它生成的图像通常描绘奶牛在牧场上吃草、猪在泥地里拱土。即使研究人员明确要求生成真实的场景，这种偏见依然存在。当研究人员关闭提示词修订功能后，生成的图像便更加接近现代畜牧业的实际饲养方式，即将农场动物饲养在室内。研究人员要求模型生成北美、欧洲和大洋洲农场的图像。结果发现，无论指定哪个地区，模型生成的图像大多呈现田园牧歌式的场景在关闭提示词修订功能后，不同地区之间的差异开始显现。通过提示词修订机制将畜牧业浪漫化，掩盖其真实状况，可能会进一步强化公众对于农场动物饲养方式的错误认知，甚至传播错误信息和虚假信息。这种现实与 AI 生成内容之间的脱节，可能会阻碍社会开展有意义的对话。研究人员警告应警惕 AI 生成图像中普遍存在的、过度美化现实的倾向。

items.title: Epic Games 计划支持尽可能多的 Linux 发行版
items.content_text: Epic Games 通讯主管 Jake Jones 表示，新 Epic Games 启动器目前处于预览阶段。Epic Games 计划支持尽可能多的 Linux 发行版，包括 Fedora、SteamOS、CachyOS、Omarchy 等，目前正在测试和评估各种打包格式，将于本月恢复对 AppImage 的支持。如果 Epic Games 支持 Flatpak 打包格式并将其发布到 Flathub 上，那么 SteamOS 用户将会很容易使用 Epic Games——只需要切换到桌面模式，然后在 Discover 应用中直接安装。

items.title: 幼儿园小学初中学龄人口已达到峰值
items.content_text: 国家发展改革委社会发展司副司长黄玮茹在周二的新闻发布会上表示，从全国层面看，目前幼儿园、小学、初中学龄人口已经达峰，高中和高等教育学龄人口还在持续增长，对资源配置提出了新的要求。十四五时期，我国幼儿园、小学、初中在校生减少将近 1700 万人。2021 年—2025 年，我国基础教育城镇和乡村在校生之比由约 8：2 提高到约 9：1，越来越多的孩子进城读书。根据教育部数据，去年全国幼儿园、小学和初中的在校生总人数约为 1 亿 8900 万人。去年中国人口出生率降至至少 1949 年以来的最低水平。与此同时 65 岁及以上老年人口突破 2 亿 2300 万人，创下历史新高。

items.title: 科学家在碲化锰观察到交替磁性证据
items.content_text: 科学家在碲化锰中观测到一种被称为“手性交替磁振子”的集体自旋运动，为交替磁性这一新型磁态提供了关键实验证据，也意味着未来芯片和信息存储技术有了新的可能。交替磁性被认为是介于铁磁与反铁磁之间的第三类磁有序。普通磁铁内部电子自旋像一排同向排列的小磁针，整体产生明显磁场；反铁磁体中相邻自旋方向相反，磁性彼此抵消。交替磁体同样没有明显外磁场，却因原子空间排列方式特殊，保留了一些通常只在铁磁体里出现的电子自旋特性，因此被寄望于开发干扰更小、更紧凑的自旋电子器件。此次实验把目光投向磁振子。材料受热或受扰后，局部自旋变化会像水波一样向周围传递，这种集体波动的量子化单位就是磁振子。理论曾预言，交替磁体中的磁振子可能带“手性”——自旋集体运动存在顺时针或逆时针的偏好，且这种偏好会随传播方向改变。

items.title: FDA 警告 GLP-1 减肥药可能增加突然失明风险
items.content_text: FDA 周一表示，GLP-1 药物生产商须在产品标签上增加一项可能导致突然失明的警示。被称为非动脉炎性前部缺血性视神经病变(nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy，NAION)的眼部疾病会影响视神经——负责将信号从眼睛传输至大脑的神经。当流向视神经的血液减少或受阻时，可能导致视力突然丧失，这种损伤是永久性的，目前无已知疗法。2024 年《JAMA Ophthalmology》期刊发表了一项研究，发现使用司美格鲁肽处方药的糖尿病患者患 NAION 的可能性是未使用该药患者的四倍。FDA 随后展开了调查，在审查了递交的副作用报告和多项临床试验的数据之后，FDA 发现所有 GLP-1 药物均出现 NAION 病例的报告。FDA 科学家尚未能明确药物导致 NAION 风险增加的具体机制。NAION 的某些危险因素，与 GLP-1 药物使用者中常见的健康状况——如 2 型糖尿病、肥胖症、睡眠呼吸暂停和高血压——存在重叠。

items.title: Ueno Is the Loneliest Number
items.content_text:
Paraguayan Bank Collapse topples the country's president. (sl Substack) Paraguay's biggest bank by customer count, the digital lender ueno bank, was seized by the central bank on November 2. Within four days President Santiago Peña had resigned, been unanimously impeached and removed, and been put under house arrest. Tomás Mandl, a former US diplomat in Paraguay and author of Modern Paraguay, argues the bank's rise was built on presidential connections and a "revolving door" between business and regulators, and that the collapse shows a democracy that is still maturing.

Background: Peña held shares in Ueno Holding, the parent of the group that owns the bank, until 2025. After taking office in 2023 he appointed Carlos Carvallo, a former chairman of the bank's predecessor, to run the central bank. Public bodies including the state pension fund deposited hundreds of millions of dollars at ueno (ABC Color, in Spanish). Mandl also credits what held up under stress: the press, a central bank supervisor, Congress, prosecutors, and a deposit guarantee of about US$38,000 per person. More on the collapse: NPR: how the collapse left millions in limbo and toppled Peña Al Jazeera explainer ABC Color, 2025: Peña's brother in an offshore shareholder of ueno (Spanish)

items.title: Democrats Win Mississippi Senate Seat as Blue Wave Comes for Everyone
items.content_text:
Democrats have done the unthinkable and flipped a Senate seat in Mississippi.

Democrat Scott Colom beat incumbent Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith with 49.19 percent of the vote, CNN projected on Wednesday, over one week after the election. Colom leads with more than 4,500 votes.

Colom will be the first Democratic senator in Mississippi in 37 years and the first Black senator in the state since Reconstruction.

In addition to her public backing of Donald Trump, Hyde-Smith really stepped in it when she encouraged people to “pick another protein” if beef was getting too expensive. The viral soundbite became the focus of one of Colom’s attack ads, where Mississippi residents said they’d rather “pick another senator.”

Colom’s victory is an astounding rebuke of the Republican Party in the Magnolia State. In 2024, incumbent Republican Senator Roger Wicker won with 62.81 percent of the vote.

Colom is a 43-year-old Black Democrat and the district attorney for the 16th judicial district in Mississippi. On the campaign trail, he argued that Trump’s tariffs and Iran war caused extreme harm to Mississippians.
